directive.quote: Every sign-in way the old sign-in had works on the new engine, one to one or better.

preserve: a password kept as a memory-hard key with its own salt, its tries limited per window
an emailed code directly under every passkey button that signs in, kept hashed, working once and dying after its tries
a texted code that needs the password too and cannot change the ways in
an authenticator app turned on only after its first right code (RFC 6238), each code signing in once
backup codes that each sign in once, new ones ending the old
a confirmed email that recovers a forgotten password
a passkey link that adds a passkey on another device
a personal key that approves a waiting app within its own scopes
ways added, changed and removed only from a recent sign-in, and the last way in never removed
allowed_deltas: the ways and their limits are the account's own lists row, written against the revision read, instead of product constants
codes go out through the Workshop tool the account picks for each channel, named by handle and run with the account's vault
codes are kept as BLAKE3 hashes
an account a place holds gets its starting rows once at its first start, and its vault is reached by name with values on pipes only
banned_substitutions: a message provider named in engine code
a secret value in a row, an argument, a file or a log
a ways row assumed when the account has none
an import from the old issuer
